stories.title: At ECO moot, Dar calls for translating 'collective commitments into concrete action'
summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar closed out the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers (COM) in Islamabad on Monday with a call for countries to translate their commitments into action.

Dar underscored Pakistan’s commitment to advancing the ECO agenda as the chair of the organisation and to working with all institutions and member states to strengthen regional connectivity, facilitate intra-regional trade and promote mutually beneficial economic cooperation.
He reiterated his government’s resolve to promote regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration within the ECO member states.

stories.title: Lawyers submit affidavits detailing Nov 11 meeting with Imran, Bushra at Adiala jail
summary: ISLAMABAD: Lawyers representing former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, have submitted affidavits to the Islamabad High Court (IHC), detailing their Nov 11 meeting with the incarcerated couple at Adiala jail.

According to the affidavits, the meeting was arranged pursuant to an order passed by the IHC on November 10, directing the jail authorities to facilitate a meeting between Imran, Bushra and their lawyers at Adiala jail.
According to the application, medical records furnished by the Adiala jail superintendent had revealed that Bushra’s eye condition required urgent medical intervention.

stories.title: Trump says 'would not mind' Huang being reinstated at Nvidia
summary: Trump also raised fresh doubts over allegations that Alice Huang, a woman with whom Huang had an affair, was spying for China after all. “I don’t know that she is a spy.

Usually what happens with that is that, any woman coming to the country that’s a beautiful woman that comes from China, they say she is a spy,” Trump said. “China plays games with us and we play games with them,” he said.
The Nvidia scandal has caused tensions in the White House over the sale of advanced American AI chips to China.

stories.title: We know how to hurt India, says Pakistan coach Solano ahead of SAFF Championship final
summary: Pakistan will face defending champions India at the National Stadium in Dhaka, Bangladesh, with the Green Shirts chasing their maiden SAFF Championship title and a landmark first appearance in the tournament’s final.
Abdul Samad Arshad scored the decisive goal in the closing stages to send Pakistan into their first-ever SAFF Championship final.
With Pakistan having played a demanding schedule during the tournament, Solano was also asked whether fatigue could become a concern ahead of the final.

stories.title: In tit-for-tat move, Chaudhry Salik sends CM Maryam, Azma Bokhari defamation notices
summary: In a tit-for-tat move, PML-Q leader and Overseas Pakistanis Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain said on Monday he has also sent a defamation notice to Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.
After the PML-Q leader levelled allegations of corruption against the incumbent Punjab government, CM Maryam sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to him, demanding he retract his remarks.

Salik’s defamation notice to Maryam, seen by Dawn and filed via Advocate Waleed Khalid, was sent over “false, baseless and defamatory” statements made by her during a public speech in Attock on Nov 3, 2026.

stories.title: Dar says Pakistan to host next Makkah alliance summit later this month
summary: Pakistan will host the next meeting of the Makkah Defence Alliance’s apex committee, likely later this month, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Monday.
Asked about regional security architecture, Dar recalled the Aug 7 signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
Islamabad has ‘not given up’ on US-Iran peace efforts DPM Dar also reaffirmed that Islamabad has not given up on its diplomatic efforts for a peaceful resolution to the US-Iran war.

stories.title: Trump says he might meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China
summary: United States President Donald Trump said on Monday he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in China this week, an announcement that could dramatically reshape his upcoming trip through East Asia if it occurs.

The president, who met the North Korean leader several times during his 2017-2021 term, including once in the Korean Demilitarised Zone, has previously expressed interest in another meeting during his current term.

We have a chance to accomplish a lot.” Trump has indicated he will meet with Putin and Xi during his trip, but US officials and analysts have played down the possibility of a meaningful agreement emerging from any trilateral sit-down.

stories.title: Shaun Tait, Kusal Mendis want extra push for Pakistan-Sri Lanka series result
summary: Sri Lankan skipper Kusal Mendis and Pakistan bowling coach Shaun Tait urged their teams to push hard for a result in the second and final Test starting on Tuesday in Rawalpindi.
Sri Lanka twice spurned chances to force a result as they let go a strong position of 404-4 in reply to Pakistan’s 434-9 declared, slumping to 446 all out.
The two-match series is part of the World Test Championship’s fourth cycle, with Pakistan (ninth and last) and Sri Lanka (seventh) already out of next year’s final.

stories.title: 'I may not return alive': In open letter to top judges, Imran pleads for medical treatment for him and Bushra Bibi
summary: In the letter, Imran detailed his own deteriorating health condition as well as his wife’s, pleading with the courts to grant them access to medical treatment. “I spent my life building hospitals so that those who could not afford treatment would receive it free of cost.

Speaking to Dawn, PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram called on the courts to take notice of Imran’s letter. “His case should also be seen on humanitarian grounds and medical treatment for him and Bushra Bibi should commence immediately,” he said.

On Aug 18, the SS directed the government to shift the jailed ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, a day after the superintendent of the Adiala jail — where Imran is imprisoned — submitted a report to the court on the ex-premier’s health condition.

stories.title: UN chief urges countries to rein in 'merciless' killer robots
summary: The United Nations chief on Monday called on countries to work towards imposing strict and binding rules on the use of “merciless” lethal autonomous weapons systems, often dubbed “killer robots”.
High stakes The meeting brings together 128 countries to decide whether to open negotiations on legally binding rules.
At the UN General Assembly last month, 163 states adopted a resolution calling for negotiations on rules governing autonomous weapons.

stories.title: IHC directs petitioner to prove ownership of Bari Imam House to CDA
summary: The court noted that the petitioner had produced no ownership documents, and that his counsel had candidly conceded that the relevant record lay with the CDA and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration.
The petitioner, by contrast, had claimed that the premises comprise a mosque, a langar khana and wuzu (ablution) facilities, and that the land was exempted shrine property never acquired by the CDA.

During the hearing, the petitioner’s counsel conceded that the property was not his own and that he was merely a caretaker of the shrine, while also stating that he did not possess the relevant documents and that they were held by the CDA.

stories.title: Trump backs potential return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Monday he would not mind seeing Jensen Huang return ‌as chief executive officer of Nvidia, adding his voice to calls for Huang's reinstatement after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy forced him out.

There's a big group of people that would like him to return." Huang is considering a comeback ​as Nvidia's CEO and has discussed with confidants the possibility of returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday.
But Nvidia's board ​was not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters.

stories.title: International media voice alarm over Israel's arrest of West Bank journalist
summary: The group representing international media in Israel and the Palestinian territories voiced alarm on Monday over Israeli forces’ arrest of an Agence France-Presse (AFP) freelancer in the West Bank, urging his release unless evidence is presented.
AFP in a statement on Sunday said it was “very concerned” about Ateeq. “We demand the Israeli authorities explain clearly why he is being detained and provide evidence.
Israeli forces in August arrested another AFP freelancer in the West Bank, Mohammed Awad.

stories.title: 13-year-old girl's murder case: Islamabad court grants police 4-day physical remand of suspects
summary: The suspects were presented before Judicial Magistrate Naima Iffat at the district and sessions court in Islamabad by police, who sought eight-day physical remand.
However, the court approved a four-day physical remand of the suspects after initially reserving its decision on the police request.

The suspects were arrested on Sunday after a first information report (FIR) was registered under Section 302 (intentional murder) of the Pakistan Penal Code at the Shams Colony police station on the complaint of the 13-year-old girl’s father.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol, high-speed diesel price by Rs2
summary: Separately, All Pakistan Petrol Pump Owners Association Vice Chairman Nouman Ali Butt wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif requesting a montlhy revision in petroleum prices instead of on a daily basis.

On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.

stories.title: I made Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad take the 10-minute park test
summary: The ten-minute park test asks whether people can reach a public park or playground on foot from their homes.
The larger-park access clusters around places such as Greater Iqbal Park, Bagh-i-Jinnah, Jilani Park and Model Town Park show the enduring value of setting aside substantial public space.
Lahore: An exploratory model estimates that 41% of mapped street and path length in Lahore district lies within an 800-metre walking route of a counted park, garden or play area.

stories.title: Symbol of neglect
summary: On the development front, as Islamabad witnesses the construction of new underpasses and bridges on a near-monthly basis, Karachi’s infrastructure crumbles under the weight of its burgeoning population, exacerbated by the governance conundrum it faces.

Whatever resources are earmarked for the city are further fragmented between the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) and provincial authorities, making coordinated urban development all the more difficult.

Karachi is not simply a poorly developed city; it is an economically indispensable one whose governance arrangements systematically undermine its capacity to convert economic activity into better urban outcomes.

stories.title: SBP says inflation to ease to 5-7pc target range during FY2027
summary: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Monday that consumer price inflation was expected to gradually ease towards the medium-term target range of five to seven per cent during financial year 2027.

Real GDP growth would remain in the range of 3.5-4.5pc, the bank said in a yearly report, which added the country’s current account deficit was likely to be in the range of 0-1pc of GDP in the financial year.

The report expected economic expansion, tariff rationalisation and higher global commodity prices to drive import growth, while exports were projected to recover moderately on the back of policy incentives and a slight increase in global demand.

stories.title: IHC directs Bari Imam House caretaker to prove land ownership in five days
summary: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday directed the caretaker of Bari Imam House to submit ownership documents for the property to the Capital Development Authority (CDA) within five days.
The judge observed that the petitioner had obtained a stay order without even knowing the area of the land on which Bari Imam House stood.

Also Read: CDA anti-encroachment drive to continue: Talal The dispute over Bari Imam House is part of a wider anti-encroachment operation launched by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) in Islamabad's Bari Imam and Noorpur Shahan areas.

stories.title: Ackerman's maiden ton lifts South Africa in first Test
summary: Marques Ackerman blasted his maiden century to put South Africa in good position against Bangladesh on the second day of their first Test at Johannesburg on Monday.
The 30-year old left-handed batsman fell for 157 off 164 balls, his first century in his third Test, to enable South Africa reach 287-4 at stumps in reply to Bangladesh’s first innings total of 400.
Litton Das, who resumed his innings at 92, fell to Dane Paterson after the wicket-keeper batsman had hit 14 fours and one six in his commanding knock.

stories.title: Pakistan look to seal series against Sri Lanka
summary: Saqib, on the other hand, despite making his Test debut relatively late in his career, displayed intelligence, exploited the pitch and conditions, and produced a superb spell that blew away Sri Lanka's batting line-up.
Saud Shakeel was the biggest positive for Pakistan in the first Test in which the hosts scored 434-9 declared and 284-8 declared.
And in the last Test match, there were some good times for batting as well.

stories.title: US airports slowly return to normal after 3 days of disruption
summary: The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks, and was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment.
Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables.
FAA chief Bryan Bedford said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday.

stories.title: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ in trilateral summit
summary: The leaders of China, Russia and the United States will discuss “world peace” when they hold their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen this week, Beijing said on Monday.
After a US-Russia bilateral treaty on nuclear weapons expired in February, Trump called for a “better agreement” including China.
Iran Trump has said the three leaders will also likely discuss his war in Iran. “We’ll talk a lot of things, including denuclearisation, but we’ll be talking a lot of things.

stories.title: Nvidia's AI financing machine may survive Huang, but with less risk appetite
summary: Nvidia's $500 billion AI financing platform is unlikely to disappear with co-founder Jensen Huang's departure, but losing its chief dealmaker could make it harder to ​bankroll some of the riskier infrastructure bets driving the AI boom.

Nvidia also provided $230 billion in financial guarantees, they said, the most recent in August when it agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion in financing to help OpenAI lease a sprawling data center in Ohio under development by SB Energy, owned by Japan's SoftBank.

Investors focus on contracts or guarantees In Nvidia's ​uncertain post-Huang future, analysts said, the new financing ​platform may shift its focus to more established ⁠hyperscalers as lenders and credit investors — who provide funds to Nvidia's partners — worry about risk.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz calls for collective efforts to tackle regional security threats in meeting with ECO FMs
summary: Welcoming the visiting dignitaries, the prime minister thanked them for attending the meeting and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the organisation’s objectives, particularly regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration.
Pakistan's assumption of the ECO chairmanship comes amid persistent regional tensions and challenges to economic integration.

Against this backdrop, Pakistan's two-year ECO chairmanship offers an opportunity to address barriers to regional trade, strengthen transport corridors and translate longstanding commitments to economic integration into practical initiatives.

stories.title: Vance 'undecided' on 2028 presidential run: report
summary: US Vice President JD Vance is reportedly “undecided” about whether to run in the 2028 presidential election and may not make a final decision until after the New Year, Axios reported on Sunday.
Speaking to Axios, unnamed sources made claims about Vance’s plans regarding the 2028 presidential race.
It was also reported that, following the midterm elections, Vance met with members of the Rockbridge Network, a large network of technology leaders and conservative donors that he helped establish.

stories.title: Meet the new 007: Robert Pattinson takes over James Bond role
summary: Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as the next James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig as the iconic British secret agent in the long-running film franchise.
The Batman and The Odyssey star will take on the role of 007 in the upcoming James Bond film, ending months of speculation over who would become the next actor to portray the legendary spy.
Pattinson's casting marks a new chapter for the James Bond franchise following Craig's departure.

stories.title: US army soldier files whistleblower complaint over Iranian strike that killed 6 service members
summary: A US Army major who survived an Iranian strike on a makeshift operations centre in Kuwait that killed six service members has filed a whistleblower complaint alleging that the Pentagon ignored concerns about inadequate protection for troops, CNN reported on Sunday.

Although senior Pentagon officials described the facility as fortified at the time, a source familiar with the site previously told CNN that its defences consisted mainly of concrete barriers designed to protect against car bomb attacks, but not necessarily drones or missiles.
The whistleblower complaint also states that the facility had neither a physician nor a permanent medical treatment station when the drone strike occurred.

stories.title: FCC conditionally allows PHC to hear cases related to PTI workers' preventive detention
summary: However, today, the bench allowed the PHC to take up the cases on the condition that the high court would not hear pleas that challenged the Oct 11 proclamation of emergency and imposition of governor’s rule in KP, where the army had also been called in aid of civil power.

The KP government urged the FCC to maintain the suspension of Article 199 proceedings instituted on or after Oct 12 throughout the province, citing ongoing security threats and law and order concerns.
He urged the FCC to grant relief, pointing out that several PTI workers and activists remained in detention following the imposition of emergency in the province.

stories.title: Nvidia set to deliver first life-after-Huang briefing
summary: The sudden departure of Nvidia's influential CEO, Jensen Huang, has shifted attention ahead of the chip giant's quarterly earnings from concerns over narrowing margins ​and use of cash to more critical questions about its influence across the AI ecosystem.
The company is due to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes on Tuesday.

"The multiple has been under pressure even prior to Huang's departure. ‌The market is ⁠evidently sceptical of those earnings' growth expectations," said Rory Dowie, London-based equity portfolio manager at asset manager Marlborough, who exited his Nvidia positions last week.

stories.title: SC grants post-arrest bail to 4 suspects in human placenta smuggling case
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court (SC) on Monday granted post-arrest bail to four suspects arrested in a case relating to the alleged illegal purchase and sale of human placentas.

Deputy Attorney General Raja Shafqat Abbasi told Dawn that, acting on credible information about the illegal collection, processing, storage and commercial trade of human placentas, a joint team of the FIA’s CCC and HOTA raided a house in Islamabad’s Sector F-7/1.

According to the preliminary investigation, the suspects were allegedly acting in connivance with one another and were involved in the illegal collection, preservation, storage, processing, packaging and export of human placentas for commercial gain.

stories.title: Senator accuses US Commerce Department of failing to stem flow of AI chips to China
summary: The Senate Commerce Committee's top Democrat has accused the Commerce Department of not doing enough ‌to prevent China from obtaining advanced AI chips, saying Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's failure to take action undermined national security.
"Despite these warnings, the Department of Commerce delayed action on repeated national security warnings, putting America's technological advantage in AI at risk," Cantwell said.
Lutnick's failure to use his authority has "undermined America's national security," ​she also wrote.

stories.title: Beyoncé reaches another major milestone in her Grammy career becoming first artist to reach 100 nominations
summary: Beyoncé has reached another landmark in her music career, becoming the first artist in Grammy history to receive 100 nominations.
The latest nomination adds to a record-breaking Grammy history that has seen Beyoncé dominate several categories over the years.
With 100 nominations now secured, Beyoncé has extended her lead in Grammy history.

stories.title: Taylor Swift reaches rare Grammy milestone with latest Album of the Year nomination
summary: Taylor Swift has added an achievement to her Grammy record, becoming only the second artist to receive Album of the Year nominations for five consecutive studio albums.
Swift received five nominations in total, taking her career tally to 63 nominations and 14 Grammy wins, according to figures reported alongside this year’s announcement.
With an Album of the Year nomination secured, Swift has further strengthened her place among the ceremony’s most decorated artists, even as a fifth victory remains uncertain.

stories.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'accelerated action' to exit fossil fuels
summary: COP31 co-host Australia released the first draft of a broad political deal on Monday that includes a call for nations to speed up the phase-out of planet-heating coal, oil and gas.
The draft decision needs ultimate approval by the nearly 200 nations at the UN climate summit in Turkiye, where the future of fossil fuels has been among the most hotly debated issues.
World is watching The draft deal also includes calls from developing countries for rich nations to triple funding for climate adaptation to at least $120 billion.

stories.title: SBP projects 3.5-4.5% GDP growth for FY27
summary: According to the report, Pakistan’s economy demonstrated resilience against domestic and global economic shocks in an increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment, recording improvements across key macroeconomic indicators in FY26.

Nonetheless, strong growth in workers' remittances contained the current account deficit at 0.1% of GDP in FY26. #SBP has released the Annual Report on the State of Pakistan’s Economy for Financial Year 2025-26.

The report notes that while Pakistan’s macroeconomic conditions have improved, deep-rooted structural reforms are needed to put the country on a sustainable high growth path to absorb the expanding working-age population.

stories.title: Pakistan face India in SAFF Cup final in Dhaka
summary: We have a lot of respect for India and football,” Pakistan head coach Nolberto Solano told a news conference in Dhaka on Monday. “We've been still making good progress in football.
The final at Bangladesh capital will be a landmark occasion for Pakistan, who have reached the tournament's showpiece match for the first time in the event’s history.
India coach Naushad Moosa has acknowledged that Pakistan will present a different challenge from the group-stage encounter, particularly following the arrival of their overseas-based players.

stories.title: Chaudhry Salik sends defamation notices to CM Maryam, Azma Bokhari amid corruption allegation row
summary: "Attempts to intimidate through legal notices will neither silence nor deter me from raising concerns on matters of public interest and their well-being," he said.
Hussain reiterated his allegations of corruption and mismanagement in Punjab, calling for accountability rather than what he described as attempts at intimidation.

I stand by it and will continue to," he said during a political talk show on a private TV channel, while responding to a question about his brother Shafay Hussain being a minister in the same Punjab government he had criticised.

stories.title: FCC conditionally allows PHC to hear cases under Article 199
summary: Read: Federal Constitutional Court bars Peshawar High Court from hearing MPO detention cases The council also requested the FCC to clarify its Nov 5 order.
Latif Khosa had informed the court that PHC proceedings in cases filed under Article 199 had come to a halt after the court’s order.

Barrister Gohar expresses disappointment Speaking to reporters after the hearing, Barrister Gohar said the PTI had again requested the FCC to allow the PHC to decide the pending petitions to grant relief to detained party workers, to no avail.
